To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DRD2/ANXK1 Taq1A (rs180049) single nucleotide variant predicts striatal D1 receptor (D2R) availability, and the difference between the TaqIA A1 allele carriers and A1 noncarriers was 5-12% lower D2R specific-binding in the striatum.
DRD2 TaqIA allele (T) carriers have reduced striatal D2 dopamine receptor (D2R) specific binding relative to noncarriers (C), regardless of body weight or diagnostic group.
the DRD2/ ANKK1 TaqIA A1 allele is associated with reduced D2R binding as assessed with [11C] NMB in both healthy controls and patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how dopamine D2 receptors in the striatum are regulated by genetic variation.
the relationship between the DRD2 gene and striatal dopamine D2/D3 receptors (D2/D _{3} R), which are important targets for antipsychotics.
the role of the ankyrin repeat and kinase domain‐containing 1 (AnkK1) gene and its TaqIA polymorphism in modulating the function of the dopamine (D2) receptor (D2R).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DRD2/ANAK1 gene polymorphism is associated with the risk of developing schizophrenia and the TaqIa polymorphism may influence the severity of schizophrenia.

the DRD2/ ANKK1 TaqIA (A1) allele is associated with lower striatal D2/D3 receptors as measured by PET with the radioligand [11C]raclopride, but not with D2 receptor binding as measured by PET using the highly selective D2 radioligand N‐[11C‐methyl]benperidol.

the TaqIA genotype of DRD2/ANXK1 is a genetic risk factor that is associated with reduced striatum D2 receptor binding, and this may be related to certain disease states such as obesity, schizophrenia and other psychiatric disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TaqIA genotype is an important predictor of striatal D(2)R specific binding, as measured by [C-11]NMB.
DRD2 TaqIA A1+ allele carriers have reduced striatal D2Rs.
TaqIA genotype is a predictor of D2R specific availability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TaqIA allele carriers have less D2R availability than noncarriers, and that this difference in D2R availability is large enough to have important clinical and biological implications.
the A1 allele is associated with reduced D2R specific availability, and this reduction is comparable to the magnitude of reduction seen with other D2/D3 radioligands.
the DRD2/ANNNK1 TaqIa polymorphism is associated with a reduction in the density of D2R in the striatum, which is the brain area most relevant to the action of antipsychotic medications.
